🖥️ Agent Interactive Terminal
Stateful PTY terminal sessions where an agent and a person share the same screen.
🌐 English · 简体中文
> One shared terminal core with two host adapters: a DeepSeek Harness bundle and a Codex/ChatGPT MCP
App. Eight `terminal_*` tools, a live shared xterm panel, and password handoff that never enters th
e model context. Seventy-seven tests pass on Linux with Node 20/22; the full design is in docs/desig
context. Seventy-seven tests pass on Linux with Node 20/22; the full design is in docs/design.zh.md.
## Why
The usual `exec` tool has no TTY. Programs do not enter interactive mode, long work is invisible, pa
sswords leak into the transcript, and a person cannot share the same shell with the model.
This project turns a terminal into a resource with identity, a screen, a phase, and a lease. The mod
el reads discrete screen snapshots instead of a byte stream; the person can take over, make it read-
screen snapshots instead of a byte stream; the person can take over, make it read-only, or seal it.
## Install
Requires Node.js 20+ and a C++ toolchain for `node-pty`. In DSH, add this index under Plugins → Disc

### Platforms
Unix shells come first: Linux and macOS use the local zsh/bash; macOS falls back to `/bin/zsh` when
`$SHELL` is unset. On Windows the launcher looks for `wsl.exe`: when usable it starts zsh (or bash i
f zsh is missing) inside WSL and translates the generated rc files to WSL paths. Without WSL it fall
s back to PowerShell 7, Windows PowerShell, or `cmd.exe`. Choosing zsh/bash without WSL fails with a
n explicit message. Native PowerShell/cmd has no prompt markers, so waits fall back to screen conten
t and output silence: usable, but less precise than WSL.

## Inside DSH
The terminal icon lives in the session header. Opening it shows an xterm panel on the right; session
tabs are numbered in their current order and close on middle click. While the agent is active, the
top bar and the area below the terminal carry an RGB running light.
- **Keyboard ownership**: typing takes the lease; a few idle seconds hand it back. Agent writes queu
e during that window, with the queued command and a cancel button in the top bar, then drain in orde

r after handback.
- **Access levels**: `collaborate`, `observe` (read-only), and `sealed` (no read o
r write; the list keeps only a redacted record). Read-only and sealed refuse queueing and return dis

tinct errors.
- **Tool policy**: interactive first by default; one-shot first and terminal only are
the alternatives. Terminal only hides bash from the agent. A separate switch steers REPL work into p

ython and similar interactive sessions.
- **Settings**: theme, font, cursor, shortcuts, scrollback,
bell, copy/paste, and lease timeout. The theme follows DSH by default and can be pinned to a fixed p
opy/paste, and lease timeout. The theme follows DSH by default and can be pinned to a fixed palette.
## Inside Codex
The same core also ships as an MCP stdio server plus a Codex plugin. After building, add the reposit
ory to Codex's plugin marketplaces:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Start `codex` and ask it to open a terminal; the `terminal_open` result carries a local panel URL. O
pen that page to share the shell, take over, make it read-only, seal it, and answer password prompts
. See docs/codex.zh.md for the full walkthrough.
The same terminal can also appear beside the conversation in the ChatGPT desktop app, which ships Co
dex as its agent. The `interactive_terminal` tool declares a `thread` entrypoint through MCP Extensi
ons; after restarting the desktop app and opening a new Codex chat, choose **Interactive Terminal**
in the side panel. The window embeds the same React panel used by the DSH adapter, with the MCP stdi
o transport adapted to the panel's attach protocol. That panel and Codex's built-in **Terminal** are
separate: the built-in one is Codex's own PTY, while Interactive Terminal drives this project's `te
rminal_*` session, with screen snapshots, waits, a takeover lease, and read-only/sealed access.

## From code
No agent framework is required; use `TerminalRegistry` directly:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`createTerminalTools(registry)` exposes the same surface to another model runtime. A password prompt
makes `wait` return `human_required` and suspends the agent; answer with `session.write(secret, { o
rigin: 'human' })`, and the secret never reaches the model. The `npm run attach` browser demo binds
`127.0.0.1` only and has no authentication; it is an example, not a deployment.
## Tools
| Tool | What it does |

| `terminal_open` | Open a session, returning id, status line, and initial screen |
| `terminal_send

` | Write text (Enter by default) and wait for a settlement |
| `terminal_wait` | Wait without writi

ng |
| `terminal_snapshot` | Read the screen or output tail, with optional row deltas |
| `terminal_

key` | Press a named key such as `ctrl-c`, `enter`, or `page-down` |
| `terminal_resize` | Resize th

e terminal |
| `terminal_close` | Close the session and its process tree |
| `terminal_list` | List
sessions, phases, sizes, and directories |
## Repository layout
One repository, one `main` branch. The session core, tools, and protocol are shared; host-specific c
ode stays in adapters rather than in a long-lived fork.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The Codex adapter imports the DSH `TerminalPanel` / `TerminalView` React component and supplies an M
CP-backed transport instead of a WebSocket. The GitHub repository is the source of truth for both ho
sts; a separate branch is only for short-lived experiments, not for maintaining the Codex port.
